items.locator: 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan — Management of Care, Legal Rights and Responsibilities, printed p.22: recognize limitations of self and others and utilize resources; provide care within the legal scope of practice. The plan measures safe entry-level nursing practice.
items.version: 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; official NCSBN/NCLEX source currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
items.stem: A newly licensed RN is asked to perform an unfamiliar procedure and has not completed the facility's required competency validation for it. The client is stable. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Perform the procedure independently because an RN license automatically establishes competence for every procedure that may be assigned in a hospital.
options.B: Delegate the procedure to assistive personnel because delegation transfers responsibility for determining whether the procedure is within the nurse's competence.
options.C: Recognize the limitation, review applicable policy, and obtain qualified supervision or competency validation before performing the procedure.
options.D: Refuse to learn the procedure permanently because unfamiliarity with a skill means the RN can never perform it within professional practice.

items.rationale: The current NCSBN test plan places recognition of one's limitations, use of appropriate resources, and practice within legal scope under Management of Care. Option C protects the client while allowing the nurse to obtain the supervision or validation needed before performing an unfamiliar procedure. Option A confuses licensure with demonstrated competence. Option B improperly shifts the issue to assistive personnel. Option D treats a current competency limitation as a permanent prohibition.

items.locator: 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan — Management of Care, Performance Improvement (Quality Improvement), printed p.22: define PI/quality-assurance activities; participate in PI projects and QI processes; utilize research/references; evaluate the impact of PI measures on client care and resource use.
items.version: 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; official NCSBN/NCLEX source currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
items.stem: A unit's fall rate has increased for three consecutive months. Which action by the staff nurse best reflects the RN's role in performance improvement?

options.A: Wait for senior administration to solve the problem because entry-level RNs do not participate in quality-improvement work involving client outcomes.
options.B: Change the fall-prevention policy independently and immediately because an individual nurse should bypass the unit's improvement process when outcome data worsen.
options.C: Participate in the structured improvement process by reviewing the data and evidence, helping test appropriate changes, and evaluating their effect on client outcomes.
options.D: Stop reporting falls until a new prevention strategy is selected because reducing the number of incident reports will make the unit's performance data more accurate.

items.rationale: NCSBN explicitly includes participation in performance-improvement projects and quality-improvement processes, use of research, and evaluation of improvement measures under Management of Care. Option C matches the entry-level RN role. Option A incorrectly excludes staff nurses. Option B bypasses the organized process and policy governance. Option D corrupts safety data rather than improving care.

items.locator: 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan — Management of Care, Performance Improvement (Quality Improvement), printed p.22: report identified client-care issues to appropriate personnel; participate in PI/QI processes; use research and references for improvement actions; evaluate impact on client care.
items.version: 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; official NCSBN/NCLEX source currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
items.stem: A staff nurse notices repeated omissions in medication-reconciliation information during transfers between units. Which response best supports quality improvement?

options.A: Report the recurring care issue through the appropriate process and participate in a structured review of causes, evidence-based changes, and outcome data.
options.B: Identify one nurse involved in the most recent transfer and treat that individual as the sole cause without examining the recurring process problem.
options.C: Ignore the pattern if no client has yet been seriously harmed because performance-improvement review should begin only after a sentinel event occurs.
options.D: Create a personal transfer form and use it without informing the unit because individual undocumented workarounds are preferable to a coordinated improvement process.

items.rationale: The 2026 NCSBN test plan expects RNs to report identified client-care issues, participate in quality-improvement processes, use evidence, and evaluate the effect of improvements. Option A addresses the repeated process problem systematically. Option B prematurely assigns individual blame, Option C delays action until harm occurs, and Option D creates an uncoordinated workaround rather than improving the care system.

items.locator: 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan — Management of Care, Performance Improvement (Quality Improvement), printed p.22: utilize research and other references for performance-improvement actions; participate in PI/QI projects; evaluate the impact of performance-improvement measures on client care and resource use.
items.version: 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; official NCSBN/NCLEX source currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
items.stem: A unit is considering an evidence-based change to its pressure-injury prevention process. Which nursing action is most consistent with the NCLEX Management of Care quality-improvement role?

options.A: Adopt the change permanently without collecting outcome data because a published intervention does not need local evaluation after implementation.
options.B: Reject the change unless every staff member already agrees with it because quality-improvement work should not proceed when practice variation exists.
options.C: Use current evidence within the organized improvement process, help implement or test the change appropriately, and evaluate its effect on client outcomes.
options.D: Keep the existing process unchanged until a serious pressure injury occurs because preventive quality improvement is not part of entry-level RN practice.

items.rationale: NCSBN's current Management of Care blueprint includes using research for performance-improvement actions, participating in QI processes, and evaluating their impact. Option C integrates all three expectations. Option A omits evaluation, Option B makes unanimous preexisting agreement a false prerequisite, and Option D incorrectly excludes preventive improvement from RN practice.

items.locator: 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan — Management of Care, Legal Rights and Responsibilities, printed p.22: recognize limitations of self and others and utilize resources; provide care within the legal scope of practice; review facility policy/legal considerations as applicable.
items.version: 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; official NCSBN/NCLEX source currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
items.stem: An RN is asked to perform an intervention that the nurse knows is outside the RN's legal scope of practice in the jurisdiction. Which action is most appropriate?

options.A: Perform the intervention once because a provider's request temporarily expands the RN's legal scope when the client needs the service.
options.B: Perform the intervention if another RN agrees to observe because peer presence converts an out-of-scope activity into authorized nursing practice.
options.C: Do not perform the out-of-scope intervention; clarify and escalate the request through appropriate channels and follow current law and facility policy.
options.D: Delegate the intervention to assistive personnel because delegation transfers the legal scope restriction from the RN to the person receiving the task.

items.rationale: NCSBN identifies practice within legal scope and recognition of professional limitations as Management of Care responsibilities. Option C is the only response that preserves legal scope while using appropriate organizational channels to resolve the client's care need. A provider request or peer observation does not expand statutory scope, and an RN cannot delegate an intervention that is outside the RN's own authorized scope to assistive personnel.

items.source_name: 2026 AHA/ACC Multisociety Guideline for Acute Pulmonary Embolism
items.locator: 2026 AHA/ACC/ACCP/ACEP/CHEST/SCAI/SHM/SIR/SVM/SVN Guideline for Evaluation and Management of Acute Pulmonary Embolism — Section 3.1.1 Clinical Assessment/Pretest Probability: validated clinical pretest-probability tools include the Wells score and Revised Geneva score and are used before definitive testing to guide the diagnostic pathway.
items.version: Multisociety acute PE guideline published 2026-02-19 and current in 2026; live guideline source rechecked 2026-08-15. Blueprint corrected to Reduction of Risk Potential because the item tests diagnostic probability assessment rather than acute physiologic management.
items.stem: A client presents with symptoms concerning for pulmonary embolism. The clinician calculates a Wells score before deciding on D-dimer testing or imaging. What does the Wells score estimate?

options.A: The short-term mortality risk after pulmonary embolism has already been confirmed by imaging.
options.B: The probability of major bleeding after therapeutic anticoagulation has been started.
options.C: The severity of right-ventricular dysfunction once pulmonary embolism is diagnosed.
options.D: The clinical pretest probability that pulmonary embolism is present before definitive imaging.

items.rationale: The 2026 multisociety pulmonary-embolism guideline uses validated pretest-probability tools such as the Wells score to estimate how likely PE is before definitive testing and to guide the diagnostic pathway. Option D states that purpose. Options A, B, and C describe prognosis, bleeding risk, or severity assessment after diagnosis rather than pretest probability. The blueprint is therefore Reduction of Risk Potential, not Physiological Adaptation.
